item.p: When: a quantifier whose copies would add more than SXML_REGEX_LARGEST_EXPANSION (256) instructions, each copy counted as at least one, compiles to a counted loop (glossary): the atom once, between COUNTED_LOOP_START (counter := 0), COUNTED_LOOP_CHOOSE, a jump out, COUNTED_LOOP_BODY (progress := position) and COUNTED_LOOP_END (counter + 1, back to CHOOSE). Smaller counts keep 's copies, which are faster (a loop pays four instructions and three backtrack entries per iteration); x*, x+ and x? are unchanged. a{2147483647} is six instructions; (?:a{1000}){1000} and (?:(?:){1000}){1000} now compile (they were LIMIT_EXCEEDED).

Matching: CHOOSE iterates below the minimum, offers an iteration as a choice below the maximum (greedy first, reluctant second, section 6.1.4) and leaves at it. Counter and progress are register slots (as progress registers are), set with RESTORE_SLOT entries like SAVE, so backtracking into an earlier iteration finds its counter, lookaround keeps working (a positive assertion keeps restoring entries), and nothing recurses (). The parameters (minimum, maximum, unbounded, reluctant, the two slots) are in a counted_loops table of the compiled regex, shared like classes by the copies of an enclosing atom: copies run one after the other and every slot change is undone in order, so they can share slots.

Empty iterations: above the minimum an iteration that consumed nothing fails, as CHECK_PROGRESS in 's unbounded loops; below it, it stands for all the iterations still needed (the counter jumps to the minimum), since each would again match nothing at the same place. This keeps (a?){2147483647}b fast and finds the same matching segments; which substring a group inside captures then is implementation-dependent (F&O 4.0, section 6.1.5).
Quantities above 4294967295 still saturate to it (cbcl-matches-004: a{99999999999999999999999999} is false, which the test allows).
